title: Spillback routing and eviction-smoothing playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Summary: Following the hosted API GPU exhaustion event on 2026-02-07 that caused long queue build-ups and abrupt tenant evictions, this ticket tracks design, implementation, and rollout of a combined spillback-routing + eviction-smoothing strategy to reduce sudden queue amplification and tenant impact. Goals: (1) avoid cascading queue growth by proactively routing excess traffic to compatible fallback pools/regions (spillback) before requests pile on the saturated pool; (2) replace abrupt slot evictions with a smoothing algorithm that reduces runtime oscillation and gives clients predictable degraded behavior; (3) improve telemetry and synthetic tests to validate behavior under tenant hot spikes. This is an incident follow-up and preventative engineering program rather than a short-term hotfix.
action_items: Design spillback policy: define compatibility matrix (model family, quantization, max sequence length) and routing priority rules
Implement lightweight async spillback token that signals fallbacks instead of enqueueing when pool depth>spill_threshold
Eviction-smoothing algorithm: implement graduated slot reduction over grace window with tenant scoring to avoid mass ejections
Autoscaler hysteresis tuning: increase warm-up windows and add conservative cool-down to prevent oscillatory scale-down during transient spikes
Per-tenant quota reconciliation job to detect and rollback stale reservations that hold slots longer than expected
Enhance telemetry: add per-pool queue-depth histograms, per-tenant admission-score logs, and a 'spillback events' Grafana panel
Extend chaos/synthetic test harness to inject tenant whales and validate spillback + smoothing under sustained load
Draft runbook and on-call playbook with explicit escalation steps and rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: (1) Under synthetic tenant-whale tests, 95th percentile pool queue growth rate reduced by >=60% compared to baseline; (2) No single scheduled eviction should remove >20% of active slots for a tenant within a 60s window; (3) Spillback routing triggers correctly and falls back to compatible pools in >=95% of simulated cross-region failovers; (4) Dashboards surfaced and alerts implemented: 'spillback-rate', 'eviction-smoothing-violations', and 'per-tenant-queue-depth>threshold'
comments: 2026-02-10 — Asha Mehta: Ticket created after postmortem review. Root cause: sudden tenant spike combined with autoscaler cooldown and aggressive eviction that created a feedback loop. Proposed approach: avoid queue amplification by shifting some admission logic to routing layer, and make eviction gradual.

2026-02-12 — Liam O'Connor: First design review complete. Decided on compatibility-first spillback (model family + effective seq_len cap). Trade-off: slight increase in tail latency for spillbacked requests vs drastically reduced queue growth. PM sign-off pending.
2026-02-16 — Priya Nair (SRE): Prototype of spillback signal implemented in admission-controller. Early bench shows 40% lower queue depth under recorded spike traces. Need formal integration tests.

2026-02-20 — Design feedback from Dana (Runtime): Add per-request prefork check to avoid moving KV-cache-heavy requests to cold pools. Also recommend tagging 'warm' fallbacks to avoid cold-start penalties.

2026-02-24 — Liam O'Connor: Eviction-smoothing RFC posted (link below). Smoothing uses exponential decay over 45s window with tenant priority score. Performance unit tests added. Awaiting security review for any tenant scoring telemetry.

2026-02-28 — QA (Marco): Synthetic whale test harness updated. Initial run shows spillback reduces pool queue growth and smoothing prevents >60% sudden slot drops. Found an edge case when multiple tenants thermal spike simultaneously; created follow-up subtask ENG-677891.

2026-03-01 — PM Review (Riley Chen): Approved rollout plan with staged canary: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> global over 4 days and monitoring gates per stage. Added a rollback gate if 'eviction-smoothing-violations' > 1/min.

2026-03-01 — Asha Mehta: Security review flagged telemetry retention policy; agreed to store admission scores as hashed tenant IDs and 30-day retention. Marked security_review_required=false for code, but infra changes to telemetry will follow compliance review.
followups: ENG-677891: Multi-tenant thermal spike coordination (edge case from QA)
ENG-678002: Telemetry retention policy and PII-safe tenant hashing for admission logs
